### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **9** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87712ab823d8c0f8d8ce0641df69f1db6be64b4c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3c28cdba3f053413901bee09662b989363d6de83` — the merge of head `23df2c8a2416b77617c8c8d47d89b2ebfb335130` into base `87712ab823d8c0f8d8ce0641df69f1db6be64b4c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3c28cdba3f053413901bee09662b989363d6de83 && git checkout 3c28cdba3f053413901bee09662b989363d6de83
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87712ab823d8c0f8d8ce0641df69f1db6be64b4c 23df2c8a2416b77617c8c8d47d89b2ebfb335130 && git checkout -B drift-repro 87712ab823d8c0f8d8ce0641df69f1db6be64b4c && git merge --no-ff 23df2c8a2416b77617c8c8d47d89b2ebfb335130

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87712ab823d8c0f8d8ce0641df69f1db6be64b4c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87712ab823d8c0f8d8ce0641df69f1db6be64b4c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `23df2c8a2416b77617c8c8d47d89b2ebfb335130`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #21829 (body and all five comments: triage, ruling B `5994120632`, claim, dev report `5999084697`, seat acceptance `5999225441`), PR #21900 (body, 12-file list, one bot comment), the net diff `origin/main...23df2c8a` (1118 insertions, 33 deletions), and the head's check-runs, latest run per name. Head source was read as git objects only. Classes, positions and functions only.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Position — right.** The narrowing lives in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`, in the write middleware's step 3, before `next()`: one more scope pushed onto the `extra` array that RLS, controlled-by-parent and the delegator scopes already compose, marked `policy` provenance and AND-ed onto `opCtx.ast.where`. Because the engine seeds its predicate path's matched-row read, per-row hook dispatch and driver write from that AST (verified at the head: `driver.find(object, ast, preOpts)` on both verbs), the narrowing binds all three. This is the seam ruling B named; no `packages/objectql` source and no kit write hook (`attachment-access-hooks.ts`, `comment-access-hooks.ts`) is in the file list.
2. **The read question — right.** `readableRowsScopeForPredicateWrite` asks the engine itself (`this.ql.find`) under the caller's context with the operation-private keys stripped (`withoutOperationPrivateKeys`, exported from core), of a copy of the caller's verbatim `options.where` (the same predicate step 2.9 guards), projecting `id` with `limit` cap plus one. Going through the engine means every read-side middleware applies, the kits' parent-derived read filters included, with no second visibility evaluator. The composed scope is `id IN (returned ids)`; an empty answer composes an empty list and matches nothing, pinned on a real SQL driver (unit) and a real booted stack (dogfood) by the equality of hidden-only with match-nothing. The by-id read question of #21812 passes the context un-stripped; the predicate one is the stricter form of the same read, not a divergence in verdict.
3. **Addressed versus nested — right.** `addressedPredicateWrite` is the twin of `addressedByIdWriteId`: excluded by `engineOperationScope` (nested), by the server-derived referential-clear marker, and the by-id/multi split is read from the engine's own dispatch predicates in `@objectstack/metadata-core` (`kind === 'multi'` only). Writes the platform issues under the caller's context keep today's answer, as the ruling settled; the hook's-own-predicate-write pin and the ablation B reading cover it.
4. **The one classifier — right.** `absentUnderCallerRead` now delegates to `readUnlessRefused`, which the predicate question shares: a declared 4xx keeps the write's previous answer, a store fault propagates with nothing written, an answer is composed. Named class: a principal holding a write grant and no read grant keeps today's reach, because the read door refuses rather than answers, so there is no read-door answer for the write to equal. That is the ruling's own text and the #21812 classification, and it is pinned.
5. **The cap — right, with one precision.** `PREDICATE_WRITE_READABLE_ID_CAP` is the spec constant `MAX_BULK_PER_ROW_HOOK_ROWS` (10 000), not a second literal; over it the write is refused with the existing `INVALID_FILTER` 400 before anything runs, following the engine's own relation-filter lowering (verified at the head: `RELATION_FILTER_ID_CAP + 1`, refuse when over). The count judged is of rows the caller can read, so the refusal discloses nothing the read door does not. Precision: the engine's existing ceiling at both predicate sites is conditional on the object having per-row hooks (`hasHooksFor`), so on a hook-less composition the new refusal reaches a predicate matching over 10 000 readable rows that was previously attempted. The changeset's second FROM → TO row states exactly that, generally; the acceptance note's "every object measured carries per-row write hooks" describes the measured composition, not the rule. Declared, so right.
6. **Fail closed — right.** A `ql` without `find` refuses the write rather than running it un-narrowed; unreachable on a real boot, and the two plugin-security doubles were given a `find` and an engine-conformant `findOne` (`assertEngineFindOnePredicate`), with `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` grown through the gate's own `--write`.
7. **H5 — right.** `ExplainInput` (`explain-engine.ts`) carries object, operation, context and an optional record id, no predicate; `security/explain` is correctly left alone.
8. **Public surface — right.** No export added or removed (`check:api-surface` inside the green `TypeScript Type Check`); new symbols are module-private; no new error code; one D3 semantic entry `18.predicate-write-unreadable-row-not-matched` beside its by-id sibling, with `registry.ts` regenerated.
9. **Docs — right.** `attachments-access.mdx`, `permissions-matrix.mdx` and `rls.mdx` state the predicate rule and the cap; the by-id `403` to `404` correction in `rls.mdx` sits in the sentence this PR extends. All public text stays at classes and positions.
10. **Pins — right.** 17 unit pins (hidden-only equality, mixed count, reader keeps 403, control, read refused, store fault, over-cap, hook's own write, by-id regression) and 12 dogfood door cells (two principal classes, two parent-derived objects plus one plain RLS object, update and delete, each with the by-id 404 regression). Ablation readings are the dev's; not re-run.
11. **Gate verdicts — right.** All seven required contexts conclude `success` on the head: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Build Docs and the three PR-claim guards are `success`. Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke, Auto Label and Check PR Size are `skipped` by design. The file list touches no governed surface; the diff is under the 5 000-line class.

### ② Semver level

Right. `.changeset/21829-predicate-write-matches-readable-rows.md` declares `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor` with the `!` banner and `@objectstack/spec: patch`, and carries `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — the same line the PR body carries. A `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `minor` is the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` enforces, and the ruling ordered exactly this shape. It is byte-for-byte the shape of the sibling `.changeset/21771-write-door-unreadable-is-not-found.md` on `main`. The body states what is refused or narrowed now, two FROM → TO rows (hidden rows not matched; the readable-over-ceiling refusal), the one-line handling for an affected caller (grant read access first; read the count as rows the caller can see; write in batches), the unchanged classes, and the ADR-0087 marker `registered predicate-write-unreadable-row-not-matched` whose D3 entry exists in the diff. `patch` on `@objectstack/spec` matches the data-only registry regeneration and the precedent. No `skip-changeset`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation: `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` outside the declared surface** — answered, right: giving the doubles a `find` made them engine doubles to the gate; the ledger grew through the gate's own `--write`, coverage up, no exemption.
- **Dev deviation: the cap is a narrowing beyond "not matched"** — answered, right: the ruling delegated "the cap" to the dev in so many words; it is declared in the changeset's FROM → TO, the matrix doc and the acceptance notes; see ① item 5 for the hook-less reach, which the changeset already covers.
- **Dev deviation: the by-id `403` correction in `rls.mdx`** — answered, right: same sentence, minimal.
- **Dev deviation: two merges of `origin/main`** — answered: mechanics; the check-runs on the merged head are the verdicts.
- **Dev deviation: an additional abstract access-gap note carried in the handback message only** — ESCALATED to the seat. That note is not among this review's inputs and the seat's acceptance record `5999225441` does not mention it. Before this PR lands, the seat records on the card, as an abstract class with its carrier (filed, or dismissed with the reason), what that note said. This does not fail the diff; it is a record the card owes.
- **`open_questions[0]`: the parent-derived read door's 2 000-row candidate window** — the seat answered A on the card; judged right under the ruling's text ("a row the read door would not return is not matched"): `READ_SCAN_LIMIT = 2_000` is a read-door property in both kits, so a predicate write on those two objects whose candidate set exceeds it writes what the read door returns, with an honest count and the kits' existing server-side warning, exactly as a read of the same predicate answers. Residual, escalated as a read-side question and not a defect of this diff: the caller sees no signal of the window on the write, as it sees none on the read; the seat states it is raised with the maintainer.
- **Out-of-scope finding: the stale by-id `403` sentence in `sharing-rules.mdx`** — answered, right: docs drift with no sentence about predicate writes; an acceptance note is the carrier Prime Directive 10 prescribes for it.
- **Premises and census** — reported holding (seam at step 2.9 / step 3; cost about 81 ms at 10 000 rows; no class (a) or (b) dependency in this repo or the console at the pin); not re-measured under the read-only rule, consistent with the ruling's own by-id census.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-21829-predicate-write-matches-readable-rows`
Reviewed-by: `session_011K3zqE8Pv1Evw5hc8tZCnN`

**VERDICT: PASS**
